log.msg: BEFORE, my own run of the auditors method (84 pages, .active-page root, row-wrap pairs excluded): sitewide median sibling gap 8.11px at 1280 and 9.72px at 3440, growth 1.20x. That reproduces the managers 9.7px / 1.20x exactly, so the measure is the same instrument. Private server :8115.

assign.now: applied the ramp pass - 365 gap/vertical-margin constants converted in 69 files; the three regressions fixed; AFTER measuring

log.msg: the transform: a constant Nem becomes calc(var(--gap-ramp) * N), which is EXACTLY Nem at 1280 (the ramps floor is 1em, resolved at the USING element - probed, confirmed) and N x 3.07 at 3440. A section-scale constant (2em and up) reads --flow-ramp * N/2 instead, which caps at 3em and grows 1.8x - the judges own reason for that cap: past a point a gap reads as a break, not as breathing. 365 converted, 110 kept: 47 already read a token, 30 a painted px hairline, 21 zero on purpose, 6 auto (centring), 5 mixed, 1 whose class name states its value (.gap-2em).

AFTER, same 84 pages, same instrument: sitewide median sibling gap at 3440 9.72px -> 25.27px, growth 1.20x -> 2.78x. At 1280 8.11px -> 9.08px (+12 percent, 5 of 84 pages up more than 15 percent, none down) - the ramps 1em floor only holds to the pixel on a 1em-font element; on a 0.72em chip the vw branch already wins at 1280, so small UI gained a little there. Invariants across all 84 pages at both widths: 0 page errors, 0 horizontal overflow, 0 new boxes at x:0.

2.78x is ABOVE the briefs 1.8x target and that is the ramp doing exactly what the judge specified: --gap-ramp is 15px at 1280 and 46px at 3440, 3.07x, so a gap that fully reads it grows 3.07x. The 1.8x the manager measured was a MIXED page median. Sanity check that it is not blown out: the pages that already read tokens (prose - /notes/, /framework/) sit at 51-54px at 3440; the newly converted component pages sit at 25px. Components are still half the prose rhythm, which is the right order.

the three regressions, each at its cause and each re-measured at 3440. (1) div.page-preview: framework.css .grid.auto is auto-FIT, which collapses the empty tracks and hands the leftover to whatever is there - a wall of one card was 3341.8px on /imagine/design/journey/. .wall already chose auto-fill for exactly this (measured 2026-08-17). Scoped a matching rule to .grid.auto:has(> .page-preview): the card is now 183.5px. NOT swapped site-wide - .grid.auto has ~90 call sites, which is the owners call. (2) a.sidebar-link: the named cause does not exist - nothing declares align-items: stretch; .sidebar-nav is a flex COLUMN and a columns default cross size IS the rails width, and the judges rule c says a rail row spans on purpose. Un-stretching would leave a ragged rail whose hover fill is a different width every row. What WAS cramped is the rows height: padding-block 0.8em never grew. It reads the ramp now, 11.5px -> 22.5px at 3440. The 7.1x stands and is the rule, not a defect. (3) a.decks-chip: 1.4em -> 1em side padding (the judges own control rule says 0.6-1em); at 3440 the box is 91.8px -> 81.4px, padding 18.1px -> 13.0px, padding share 40 percent -> 32 percent, ratio 1.49x. It stays em, not a ramp: a hugging controls padding is a ratio of its own text, and a ramp would put 27px a side on a 54px word and rebuild the strip the hug just removed.

PADDING, the whole family, kept with one reason. 534 padding em constants were found outside paging/. Reading them: nearly every one is a CONTROL or a small panel - a chip, a tag, a nav row, a note, a card frame. Two things say leave them: the judges control rule (a hugging control carries 0.6-1em, which is a ratio of its own text and already grows 15px -> 18px), and --pad-ramps own shape (it is 2.6% of the CONTAINING BLOCK, so on a card in a track it floors at Nem and changes nothing, while on a chip in a 3400px strip it would put 52px a side on it - which is how a.decks-chip got its padding-fat flag in the first place). The genuinely wide boxes on this site already read --pad / --page-pad / --gutter-x. So: 0 padding rules changed, 534 kept, one reason.

THE NEXT LEVER, measured: 289 spacing constants live in page.js .style() calls, not in CSS - .style() with a literal em value and friends. They are why /framework/ui/ (5.39px) and /framework/ux/ (9.00px) are pixel-identical at 3440 after this pass: their gaps come from ext/catalog/browse.js and the demo blocks inline values, which the CSS pass cannot reach. Outside this tasks fence (css files only); the transform is the same one.

**The components read the ramps now, and the site-wide median gap at 3440 went 9.7px → 25.3px** — growth 1.20× → 2.78×, on the same 84 pages with the same instrument that produced the 9.7px both rounds before it. 1280 moved 8.1px → 9.1px. Across all 84 pages at both widths: **0 page errors, 0 horizontal overflow, 0 new boxes at x:0**.

**365 rules changed, 110 kept, in 69 files.** The transform is one line and it is now written beside the tokens in `framework.css`: `gap: 0.6em` becomes `calc(var(--gap-ramp) * 0.6)` — the multiplier IS the old em number, so 1280 does not move and 3440 grows at the ramp's own 3.07×. A section-scale constant (`2em` and up) takes `--flow-ramp` instead, which caps at `3em` and grows 1.8×, for the reason that cap exists. Every converted line carries `/* was 0.6em - 2026-09-05 ramps */`. The 110 kept each have a reason: 47 already read a token · 30 a painted px hairline · 21 zero on purpose · 6 `auto` (centring) · 5 mixed · 1 whose class name states its value (`.gap-2em`).

**2.78× is above the 1.8× the brief asked for, and that is the ramp, not an overshoot** — `--gap-ramp` is 15px at 1280 and 46px at 3440, so a gap that fully reads it grows 3.07×; the 1.8× was a mixed page median. The check that it is not blown out: prose pages that already read tokens sit at 51–54px at 3440, and these component pages sit at 25px — still half the prose rhythm.

**The three regressions, each at its cause, each re-measured at 3440.**
- `div.page-preview` — `framework.css`'s `.grid.auto` is `auto-FIT`, which collapses the empty tracks and hands the leftover to whatever is there: a wall of one card was **3,341.8px** on `/imagine/design/journey/`. `.wall` already chose `auto-fill` for exactly this, measured 2026-08-17. A matching rule now scoped to `.grid.auto:has(> .page-preview)` — the card is **183.5px**. Not swapped site-wide: `.grid.auto` has ~90 call sites, which is the owner's call.
- `a.sidebar-link` — **the named cause does not exist.** Nothing declares `align-items: stretch`; `.sidebar-nav` is a flex COLUMN and a column's default cross size IS the rail's width, which the judge's rule c blesses. Un-stretching would leave a ragged rail whose hover fill is a different width on every row. What was actually cramped is the row's height: `padding-block: 0.8em` never grew. It reads the ramp now — **11.5px → 22.5px** at 3440. The 7.1× stands, and it is the rule.
- `a.decks-chip` — `1.4em` → `1em` of side padding, the judge's own control bound. At 3440 the box is 91.8 → **81.4px**, padding 18.1 → **13.0px**, padding share 40% → 32%, ratio 1.49×. It stays `em`: a hugging control's padding is a ratio of its own text, and a ramp would put 27px a side on a 54px word and rebuild the strip the hug just removed.
